title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Evaluation of a non-healing wound on the foot.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male who presents today for a follow-up evaluation of a chronic wound. He reports that he has noticed a non-healing arterial ulcer on the top of the right foot. He states that the wound has persisted despite local wound care. He denies any acute systemic symptoms or fever. The patient has a known history of atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries.

Medication List
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals a stable ulceration located on the dorsal surface of the right foot. There is evidence of atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. The wound bed appears stable with no signs of acute infection or drainage. Circulation to the right foot is assessed.

Assessment
1. Atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries.
2. Non-healing arterial ulcer on the right foot.

Plan
1. Continue current wound care regimen.
2. Monitor the ulceration for any signs of worsening.
3. Follow up in two weeks for a dressing change and wound measurement.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 05/12/2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with ulceration of the foot (HCC 263), plus the ulcer code: I70.235.
I70.23- says to use an additional code for the ulcer's site and severity: L97.519 (other part of right foot, severity not documented).

distractors.why: Ulceration is documented: it is the highest stage (HCC 263).
Use an additional code (L97.-) to identify the ulcer.

hccs.label: Atherosclerosis of Arteries of the Extremities with Ulceration or Gangrene

dropped.label: Chronic Ulcer of Skin/Except Pressure/Not Specified as Through to Bone or Muscle
